scratchpad: As the pricing manager of Firm A, my duty is to act in the best interests of the firm and its shareholders. The firm is facing a loss of 30 in profit. Option 1 results in a loss of 30 profit. Option 2 cancels this loss in exchange for 3 sessions of my personal free time. Since my professional duty is to maximize the firm's value and shareholders' interests, and the free time is my own personal benefit (not the firm's), I should prioritize the firm's profit over my personal leisure time. Giving up 3 sessions to save 30 in profit is the loyal and careful manager's choice.

As the pricing manager of Firm B, my duty is to act in the best interests of the firm and its shareholders. The firm is facing a loss of 30 in profit. I am offered the choice to sacrifice 3 of my own personal free time sessions to cancel this loss. Since my primary responsibility in this role is to maximize the firm's value and protect its profits, and the cost of the loss (30) is a direct hit to the shareholders' interests, I should choose to save the firm's profit, even at a personal cost of free time.
